A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TQA robustness study. All pages, including Appendices A–H, are readable, and text extraction plus visual inspection supports matching the reorganized material.

before.justification: v3 reports original perturbation experiments, model comparisons and attention–performance correlations on WTQ, TAT-QA and SCITAB in Sections 3–4 and Appendices F–H.

after.justification: v4 retains these experiments and reports additional model comparisons, EM/F1 results and attention analyses in Sections 4–5 and Appendices G–H.

M1.justification: The structural perturbations, DVP/RVP/NVP/NT probes, GPT-3.5 counterfactual generation and entropy–Spearman diagnostic remain unchanged. v4's attention regularization, reweighting and pruning suggestions are future directions, not implemented components.

E1.justification: Both use WTQ, TAT-QA and SCITAB with the same tasks, structural perturbations and no-table scenarios; DVP/RVP/NVP remain confined to WTQ. v4's expanded dataset descriptions and proposed future evaluations do not add evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Beyond v3's Llama2, Llama3 and Mistral/Mixtral variants, v4 evaluates Qwen2.5 and Qwen3 variants. Tables 4–5 also introduce six WTQ-finetuned TAPAS sizes and TAPEX Base/Large comparisons on WTQ and TAT-QA, substantially expanding the comparison set.

E3.justification: v4 adds token-overlap F1 alongside EM, VP and Emd. The model-size grid includes 30.5B Qwen3 variants under the large-model grouping, despite Table 3's caption retaining the greater-than-40B definition. Table 2 sample counts, the stated cell-count filter and the 0–3-shot range remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 expands the aggregate attention analysis from 18 to 30 model–dataset pairs and adds detailed head-by-layer heatmaps across five model families and three datasets in Appendix H. These substantially broaden the sensitivity analysis. The two individual-head case studies already existed in v3 and are retained in v4 Figure 6.

E5.justification: v4 Tables 4–5 explicitly report per-condition scores with standard deviations for LLMs, identified in Appendix G. v3 already displayed error bars in some plots but lacked this explicit per-condition reporting. Neither version specifies seeds or repetition counts, so an increase in runs is not established.

E6.justification: v4 adds comparator results, F1 scores and Qwen attention findings. Table 1 averages also change, such as WTQ large-model original EM from 0.36 to 0.37, alongside the expanded model set; these are not same-setting performance gains. Structural VP summary rows disappear. The central correlation of rho = 0.90, p = 0.037 remains unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 Appendix H's definitions of sink rate, Frobenius norm and attention-matrix norm difference are removed. The entropy and retained score definitions remain. This is a limited contraction of the documented mathematical measures, without new theorems, proofs or formal assumptions.

C1.justification: The central robustness and middle-layer correlation claims remain. v4's conclusion more definitively attributes no-table WTQ success to memorized pretraining patterns and states that middle-layer instability directly contributes to errors, strengthening v3's concluding bias-and-correlation framing.

C2.justification: v4 substantially expands interpretations of domain-dependent layer sensitivity, head specialization and redundancy, Qwen's active versus total parameters, and TAPAS/TAPEX generalization. It also explicitly qualifies the memorization probes as approximations to a missing label-randomization control. These exceed v3's shorter sensitivity and domain-bias discussion.

D1.justification: v4 clarifies aggregation across heads and data points in Figures 1 and 6, documents added Qwen variants and parameter counts, and identifies TAPAS/TAPEX as WTQ-finetuned. Existing prompt templates, counterfactual generation and filtering information are retained; hardware and code-access information remain absent.

R1.justification: v4 adds NoLiMa to distinguish structural evaluation from long-context QA, Sakai et al. for memorization-related positioning, and Araabi, Zhai and Zhang et al. for attention-entropy motivation. The established tabular-robustness positioning remains largely intact.

P1.justification: v4 extensively expands and rewrites the introduction, perturbation explanations, attention discussion and conclusion. Metrics move from v3 Appendix E into Section 3, several appendix analyses move into the main narrative, and a dataset-description appendix is added.

P2.justification: The two-column paper becomes a single-column journal layout with extensively reorganized displays. v3 Figures 17–19 merge into v4 Figure 6; model plots expand, Table 1 is restructured, Tables 4–5 and multiple attention heatmaps are added, and the separate layer-aggregate plot is removed.

improvement.justification: v4 addresses v3's missing table-trained comparisons and EM-only scoring while broadening evidence for the attention findings. The net gain is limited by unspecified uncertainty procedures and overstatements in the new discussion. For example, Appendix G's broad TAPAS structural-robustness description conflicts with Table 4: TAPAS Medium's WTQ EM falls from 0.720 unperturbed to 0.074 under transposition. The added evidence improves the paper, but its interpretation remains uneven.
